text:
maria: heads up — got an escalation from a customer (acct: acme-qa) hitting intermittent 401s on API requests. they say it started after they rotated keys yesterday.

devon: reproducible for them? any logs / sample jwt? :thinking_face:

maria: they supplied a sample token and we observed signature validation errors in our auth logs. sometimes succeeds, sometimes fails for the same token within a minute.

samir: that smells like JWKS caching + key rotation race. our JWKS cache default TTL is 10m, but we also have background refresh every 5m. if they rotated and the kid changed, some nodes might still use the old keys.

liz: can you paste the jwt header/kid and the error? also which backend returned the 401 (api-gateway, verifier svc)?

maria: gateway returned the 401. here are redacted bits:

```
Header: {"alg":"RS256","kid":"key-2026-rot1"}
Error: signature verification failed (kid mismatch / no matching public key found)
Log: verifier.lookup_jwks(kid=key-2026-rot1) -> cache_miss -> fetched_jwks(contains key-2026-rot2) -> still no match -> reject
```

devon: hmm fetched JWKS contains only the new key (rot2) but not rot1. that explains it — token signed with old key, new JWKS doesn't publish old key. If some nodes validated against an older cached JWKS that still had rot1, they'd accept. The intermittent success is because different verifier instances have different cache states.

samir: customer rotated keys and didn't publish the old key alongside the new one (no dual-publish/grace period). best practices are to publish both until old tokens expire or perform a smooth rollover.

liz: agreed. but we should be resilient regardless. suggestions: on signature error where kid not found, trigger an immediate JWKS refresh and retry validation once. also log a diagnostic metric for "jwt_retry_after_jwks_refresh".

maria: they already tried re-issuing token and same problem occurred for a subset of requests. i'm drafting repro steps for SE.

sre-bot: deploy pipeline notice — we rolled verifier v3.8.1 12h ago that changed jwks-cache default ttl from 10m -> 15m (was intentional for load reduction).

devon: that makes it worse — longer TTL increases window for stale keys. we should revert or make the TTL adaptive.

samir: other edge: clock skew. a token can be rejected for nbf/exp if client's clock is off. but this case is signature-specific.

maria: reproduction steps i'm including for support:
1) create key pair A, publish JWKS with kid=A
2) issue token signed with A
3) rotate: publish JWKS with kid=B only (no A)
4) send requests to multiple verifier instances rapidly — some will have cached old JWKS, some will fetch new one -> intermittent accept/deny

maria: sample curl to fetch jwks and token

```
# fetch jwks
curl -sS https://idp.acme.example/.well-known/jwks.json

# decode header
echo "<JWT>" | cut -d. -f1 | base64 -d | jq .
```

liz: for product-facing resolution we should recommend to customer:
- publish both keys for at least token_max_lifetime (or until old tokens expire)
- rotate with QA window and monitor jwt_verification_errors

devon: for our side: immediate mitigations:
- on signature failure where kid present but not matched, force async JWKS refresh and attempt 1 retry
- instrument metrics and alert if >5% of jwt_validations are failing with "kid_not_found" in a 5m window for a tenant
- consider lowering jwks-cache ttl for multi-tenant idps that rotate frequently

samir: let's be careful with the retry logic to avoid DoS against idp if they are rate-limited. add exponential backoff and a per-tenant refresh cooldown (e.g., 30s) and circuit-breaker.

maria: i'm going to file a support ticket update with recommended steps and ask them to republish the old key temporarily. cc @devon @samir

liz: also add a KB entry for key rotation gotchas and our recommended verifier config. i'll draft it.

devon: followup engineering action items:
- implement one-time JWKS refresh+retry on signature failure (devon)
- add metrics + alert (samir)
- revert jwks-cache ttl change in next patch if load tests allow (sre team)

samir: quick note on clock skew: we accept a 2m skew for nbf/exp checks. ops reported a couple tokens rejected with exp too early — those were clients with bad clocks (IOT devices). add that to KB too.

maria: customer confirmed they'll republish old key for 24h and will monitor. i'll keep thread updated.

sre-bot: incident note saved to ops/rotations with tag: jwks-intermittent-2167600000

maria: thanks all. once devon puts a PR up ping here and i'll validate with the customer's test harness.

devon: will do — aiming for PR today. :thumbsup:
